---
title: Spring
description: Quenty-style damped harmonic oscillator spring for scalar value animations
---

import { Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Overview

Spring provides a damped harmonic oscillator implementation for smooth scalar value animations. It uses fixed-timestep semi-implicit Euler integration for stable physics simulation with configurable frequency and damping ratio.

Unlike the Spr library, this Spring implementation offers direct control over physics parameters and manual update control.

## Usage

### Basic Spring Animation

```lua
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local Spring = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.Spring)

-- Create a spring with initial value, frequency, and damping
local spring = Spring.new(0, 2, 0.8)

-- Set target and run animation
spring:setTarget(100)
spring:run()

-- Read current position each frame
RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
    print('Current value:', spring.position)
end)
```

### UI Element Animation

```lua
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local Spring = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.Spring)
local RunService = game:GetService('RunService')

local button = script.Parent
local spring = Spring.new(1, 3, 0.7) -- scale from 1, fast response, slight overshoot

local uiScale = Instance.new('UIScale')
uiScale.Parent = button

-- Animate on hover
button.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
    spring:setTarget(1.1)
    spring:run()
end)

button.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
    spring:setTarget(1)
    spring:run()
end)

RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
    uiScale.Scale = spring.position
end)
```

### Impulse for Bounce Effects

```lua
local Spring = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.Spring)

local spring = Spring.new(0, 2, 0.4) -- low damping for bounce

-- Apply sudden velocity for bounce effect
button.Activated:Connect(function()
    spring:impulse(50)
    spring:run(0.5) -- run for 0.5 seconds
end)
```

### Timed Animation with Cleanup

```lua
local Spring = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.Spring)

local spring = Spring.new(0, 1, 1)

-- Animate for exactly 2 seconds then auto-stop
spring:setTarget(360)
spring:run(2)

-- Or manual control
spring:run()
task.wait(1)
spring:stop()
```

## API Reference

### Constructor

```lua
function Spring.new(initial: number, frequency: number?, damping: number?): Spring
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `initial` | `number` | required | Starting position value |
| `frequency` | `number?` | `1` | Oscillation frequency (higher = faster) |
| `damping` | `number?` | `1` | Damping ratio (`<1` = underdamped/bouncy, `=1` = critically damped, `>1` = overdamped) |

### Methods

#### setTarget

```lua
function Spring:setTarget(target: number)
```

Sets the target position the spring will move toward.

#### impulse

```lua
function Spring:impulse(velocity: number)
```

Adds instantaneous velocity to the spring for bounce/jolt effects.

#### update

```lua
function Spring:update(dt: number)
```

Manually advance the simulation by `dt` seconds. Used for fixed-timestep integration.

#### run

```lua
function Spring:run(duration: number?)
```

Starts the automatic simulation loop. Optionally auto-stops after `duration` seconds.

#### stop

```lua
function Spring:stop()
```

Stops the automatic simulation loop.

#### reset

```lua
function Spring:reset(position: number)
```

Resets spring to a position with zero velocity. Target also updates to this position.

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `position` | `number` | Current spring position |
| `velocity` | `number` | Current spring velocity |
| `target` | `number` | Target position the spring moves toward |
| `frequency` | `number` | Oscillation frequency |
| `damping` | `number` | Damping ratio |

## Spring Physics Parameters

### Frequency

Controls how fast the spring responds to target changes:
- `0.5` - Slow, heavy feel
- `2` - Quick, responsive
- `5` - Very fast, snappy

### Damping Ratio

Controls oscillation behavior:
- `< 1` (0.4-0.7) - Underdamped: bounces before settling
- `= 1` - Critically damped: fastest settling without overshoot
- `> 1` (1.2-2) - Overdamped: slow, heavy, no overshoot

## Best Practices

- **Use `run(duration)` for one-shot animations** — automatically stops to save performance
- **Use `impulse()` for reactive feedback** — button presses, impacts, notifications
- **Match frequency to UI feel** — buttons need fast response (~3), large panels can be slower (~1)
- **Read `spring.position` on RenderStepped** — only access when needed, not every frame if unnecessary
- **Call `stop()` when hidden** — springs continue running until stopped or garbage collected
- **Prefer higher damping for production UI** — slight overshoot looks playful but can feel unpolished
